messages:
Ops-Bot: :rotating_light: Paging: cont-batcher p99 spike in us-west2 (svc: text-gen), SLO breach >2x for last 5m. auto-escalate to oncall
Aria: on it. seeing stream stalls too? p95 up ~300ms, p99 jumping to 3.8s. which pool is hot?
Matt: looks like cont-batcher nodes in pool-gpu-3 (gpu:g5x) - logs show bunch of large seqs (~>8k tokens) mixed with tiny ones. batching windows are coalescing bad combos.
Sophia: yep mixed-seqlen amplification. KV cache eviction spikes at same time: "evict_count" goes up, then latency follows.
Kevin: can we quick-route streaming requests to direct-path to avoid batching? runtime flag exists: `runtime.stream_direct=true` for the service.
Jules: I can flip that for the routing policy for the next 30m if we want to buy time. downside: CPU cost goes up but reduces tail.
Aria: do it. runbook step 4: flip streaming path and drop max_cont_batch_size down to 16. Matt/Kevin, confirm commands?
Matt: running patch now. command I'm using: ```bash
infractl route update --svc text-gen --route streaming --policy direct --ttl 1800
infractl config set --svc text-gen cont_batch.max_size=16
```
Sophia: applying `cont_batch.max_size=16` on pool-gpu-3. also bumping `batch_split_threshold=512` to avoid very large joins.
Ops-Bot: deployment event: route update succeeded (route id r_93f)
Matt: changed max_size and route. watching metrics. p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 1.6s in ~90s. p95 back under SLO.
Liz: customer-impact check: we see ~4% of requests timed out (>=10s) during spike window (12:03-12:08). list of affected customers includes tenant-42 and tenant-proto (low-confidence). Raising to CS for notif?
Aria: yes please create support ticket with incident tag, mention partial request loss and mitigation steps.
Jules: long-term: we should add run-time small-first scheduling policy so tiny requests don't get paired with huge ones. current scheduler is size-agnostic age-first. propose `size-aware-fairness` with 3 bins (tiny/medium/large).
Kevin: agree. quick experiment: `scheduler.policy=size_aware` with `bins=[0-256,257-2048,2049-8192]` and `max_wait_ms=40` for tiny bin.
Sophia: note: KV cache eviction likely caused by huge sequences thrashing cache. suggestion: 1) enable per-request kv pinning for streaming (avoid evicting active contexts), 2) implement early-shed for requests > 6k tokens to route to a low-throughput high-memory pool.
Matt: opening a ticket for model routing rules: route large sequences to high-kv-capacity pool (gpu-ec).
IncidentBot: Incident created: INC-2026-3498, severity: P2, owner: Aria.
Aria: handoff to oncall3 (Kevin) at 14:00 UTC for follow-up (long-term config + postmortem). I will annotate timeline and customer list.
Kevin: taking handoff. next steps: collect sample traces (trace ids in logs), run replay on dev pool with mixed seqs to reproduce, and prototype `size_aware` scheduler in staging.
Liz: CS notified tenants with temporary mitigation note and ETA for postmortem.
Jules: for immediate safety we should add a guard: auto-threshold for cont-batching: if p99 > 2s for 3 consecutive mins then reduce cont_batch.max_size by 50% and enable direct streaming. we can implement as a temporary rule in console.
Aria: agreed. create a short-lived automation and a follow-up RFC for permanent scheduling policy.
Matt: saved traces: `/var/log/contbatch/traces/1779998886-spike.log` — contains 20 representative traces, sample config attached.
Sophia: notes for postmortem: cause = mixed sequence length amplification + KV thrash + scheduler size-agnosticness -> mitigation = route tweak + batch size reduction + proposed size-aware scheduler + KV pinning.
Aria: thanks team. handoff complete. I'll draft incident timeline and assign owners for the action items. :white_check_mark:
